errors.english: #### Chapter 61: The Account of the Farmer
errors.why: This is the closing colophon of chapter 61 (continuing 'ces pa dge ba'i dbang pos byas pa'i byang chub' from the previous side); the verses that follow open the next chapter (62), not the Farmer chapter.

fix.find: #### Chapter 61: The Account of the Farmer
fix.replace: [Colophon closing Chapter 61, The Account of the Farmer; the next chapter begins after it]

note: The verses are rendered faithfully enough, but the chapter colophon is presented as a heading, so the new story about Suprabuddha is mislabelled as the Farmer chapter.

errors.english: an endless jewel that cures fevers
errors.why: mtha' yas is the serpent king Ananta: the stock example of the fever-curing jewel of the nāga, not an 'endless jewel'.

fix.find: an endless jewel that cures fevers
fix.replace: the fever-curing jewel of the serpent king Ananta

errors.english: The purpose of the expression does not render its subject matter nonexistent.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the purpose of the expression does not occur without its subject matter existing.

errors.english: Why then must it state the purpose of the subject matter?
errors.why: ci ste introduces a view reported from Dharmottara (closed by zhes zer ba lta bu'o on the next side), that the opening statement necessarily states the purpose of the subject matter; the English turns it into a question and then presents the conclusion 'Therefore, it is certain...' as the author's own.

note: Follows the dense argument about the purpose of the opening statement reasonably well, but mistranslates the Ananta jewel example and blurs the reported view of Dharmottara at the end.
A faithful rendering of the word-glosses on the bath-powder simile, the second-dhyāna formula and the spring/lake simile.

errors.english: cognitions such as "cook" would also be erroneous
errors.why: 'khrul pa here is logical deviation (vyabhicāra): the reason is shown inconclusive by cognitions such as 'cook'; those cognitions are not said to be erroneous.

fix.find: cognitions such as "cook" would also be erroneous
fix.replace: the reason would also be deviant (inconclusive) with respect to cognitions such as "cook"

errors.why: rjes su 'jug pa'i shes pa (anuvṛttapratyaya) is the recurrent or common cognition of sameness across individuals, not a temporally consecutive cognition.

errors.english: having excluded a universal, some slight alternative cause exists
errors.why: The contrast with khyad par sgrub na ('if one proves a specific one') shows the sense is 'if one proves in general that some other cause exists'.

note: The overall dialectic against the universal 'cook-ness' is followed, but logical terms (anuvṛtti, vyabhicāra) are misrendered, which misleads the reader on the argument.

errors.why: chos kyi mchog is the fourth stage of the path of preparation, the supreme mundane quality (laukikāgradharma), following warmth, peak and patience.

fix.replace: At the stage of the supreme mundane quality (laukikāgradharma)

errors.why: In this dilemma the first horn is dismissed as merely arbitrary (cf. 'dod pa'i dbang gis below): calling the aspirational stage 'ultimate' is mere assumption, not something the author accepts.

errors.english: depends on wishing for bodily perfection and other virtues
errors.why: The point of the vase simile is that the desired things (bodily perfection, etc.) depend on this abandonment of faulty discipline, not that the abandonment depends on wishing for them.

note: The polemic and the Gaṇḍavyūha similes mapped onto the path stages are mostly followed, but a path-stage name is mistranslated and two clauses are misconstrued.

errors.why: yan lag mchog (uttamāṅga) means 'head'; the plural refers to heads adorned with the scattered garlands, not to the Buddha's 'supreme limbs'.
The Tibetan reads ārāt as 'nearby': the Sugata was then seen close at hand.

note: A good verse rendering of the Buddha's appearance on the lotuses, with a couple of minor inaccuracies.
A faithful rendering of the commentary on the novice's rules on householder dress and robe colours, with correct Vinaya terminology.

errors.english: the minds of the gods are not conquered by beings such as us
errors.why: lha here is the ministers' address to the king ('Your Majesty'): the king's mind is not to be overruled by people like us.

fix.find: the minds of the gods are not conquered by beings such as us
fix.replace: Your Majesty's mind is not to be overruled by people such as us

errors.english: Stop requesting the gift of my flesh
errors.why: sbyin stsol ba is the king's bestowing: the ministers ask him to give up bestowing his own flesh, not to stop requesting it.
rko long gsol ba means presuming to interfere or remonstrate (the ministers' objection), not becoming resentful.

note: The commentary's word-glosses are mostly right, but the ministers' address to the king is misread as referring to the gods, which garbles who says what in this passage.

errors.english: These enter through the path of the person's birth canal
errors.why: The offender enters through the birth canal of those blazing iron cows and mares, into their bellies full of blazing coals; the iron animals do not enter him.

fix.find: These enter through the path of the person's birth canal
fix.replace: He enters them through their own birth canal

errors.english: a man who forces another man into sexual misconduct
errors.why: The Tibetan describes a man engaging in sexual misconduct with a man; it says nothing about force.

note: Generally accurate on the hell punishments for sexual misconduct, but one passage reverses who enters whom.

errors.english: why is the world meaninglessly caught in existence (samsara)?
errors.why: As in Bodhicaryāvatāra 8.69, the question is why worldly people pointlessly smear the body with perfumes; srid pa here is not samsāra.

fix.find: why is the world meaninglessly caught in existence (samsara)?
fix.replace: why do worldly people pointlessly [perfume it]?

note: A faithful rendering of the commentary on the impurity of the body, apart from one misread rhetorical question.
